newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macquarie's Puma to raise A$500 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macquarie's Puma to raise A$500 mln.

text.p: Macquarie Bank Ltd said on Thursday its PUMA securitisation division would issue A$500 million of bonds.
The bonds would represent Series B of PUMA's P-5 Masterfund. Series A, which was issued in May, was worth A$800 million.
The new series would be issued in four tranches and tranches one to three will be rated AAA by Standard & Poor's and Aaa by Moody's Investors Service.
The bonds would be priced on September 24 and settled on September 30.
Bain Capital Markets is lead manager and Macquarie Bank is co-manager, said PUMA's managing director, Tony Gill.

Tranche 1F would be fixed and would represent 60 percent of the entire issue with a face value of A$300 million and tranche 2 would be floating rate and represented 30 percent with a face value of A$150 million.
Tranches 3 and 4 would be floating rate bonds with a face value A$25 million each. Tranche 4 would be subordinated bonds and would be rated AA minus rating by S&P.

"We believe the structure of the P-5 Master Fund meets the needs of both bonds investors, who are looking for flexibility and high quality investments, and of mortgage managers, who are keen to expand their books," said PUMA Treasurer Kieran Brush.
The structure of the transaction allows, through its strategic alliance with Aussie Home Loans, Australia's largest non-bank home lender, to settle redraw mortgages, Brush added.
Redraw mortgages allow borrowers to borrow extra money from their mortgage when they have made extra payments on their loans.
"The flexibility available to borrowers through this product means that Aussie Home Loans is now extremely competitive in terms of both price and service," Gill said.
The new issue would bring PUMA's outstanding issuance to A$3.508 billion. --Sydney newsroom 61-2 373-1800
